quirks: The 1890 federal census was destroyed nationally — no Benson County 1890 census exists. The 1885 Dakota Territory census and 1900 federal census are the bracketing enumerations.

County-level birth registration began in the late 1890s at the Benson County Courthouse (Clerk of District Court, Minnewaukan); statewide registration began in 1907 with general compliance only by 1924. A birth registration for November 1898 may exist at county level but is not confirmed digitized.

Statewide marriage registration did not begin until 1925. Pre-1925 marriages are at the county courthouse or in FamilySearch collection 2550852 (North Dakota County Marriages 1872-1958). Benson County is NOT in the North Dakota State Archives online pre-1925 marriage index — go to the county courthouse or FamilySearch collection directly.

Naturalization volumes at FamilySearch (imageGroupNumbers 007785641-007785645) are full-text searchable but 0% name-indexed — use FamilySearch full-text search, not the standard name index. Post-1906 petitions name the petitioner's wife and minor children, making them a direct parentage source.

Flora and Esmond Lutheran church records are only 34-36% name-indexed; roughly two-thirds of each volume must be browsed image-by-image. Both contain Norwegian-language entries — the researcher must be able to read Norwegian or obtain translation assistance.

The Spirit Lake (Devils Lake) Reservation at Fort Totten occupies the southeastern portion of Benson County. Fort Totten Agency records (birth, death, probate, census) are separate from county civil records and are held in distinct FamilySearch volumes (008271676, 008273622).

Benson County's neighboring counties — Eddy, Nelson, Pierce, Ramsey, Towner, Wells — should be searched for family records predating the Maddock settlement. Ramsey County (Devils Lake) is immediately east and was a parent county of Benson.

The FamilySearch collections_search tool timed out twice during this survey — consult the FamilySearch Catalog directly at familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/results?count=20&q.place=North+Dakota+Benson for any additional microfilm-only collections.
No courthouse fire or record loss is reported for Benson County — records from 1883 onward should be substantially intact at the courthouse.
Death certificates filed after 1923 name the deceased's parents; searching forward from 1920 for a parent death certificate is a valid strategy for identifying Reuben Spriggs's parents.
BLM homestead patent records (glorecords.blm.gov) will name the Spriggs father if he filed a homestead entry in Benson County — this is a high-yield free source for confirming identity and location.

narration.text: genealogy MCP server at session start: connected — tools available
A project already exists. Let me query the current state before routing.
The project has an objective but no questions yet. Routing to question-selection.
Question written. No locality entry exists for Benson County, North Dakota — routing to locality-guide before planning.
Locality guide written as loc_001. Now routing to research-plan.
Good — I have the locality guide. Now I'll survey available collections for Benson County and nationally before writing the plan.

Collections_search timed out (locality guide noted this as a known issue). Working from loc_001's collections list plus known major FamilySearch census collections. Let me check external links and confirm the standard place.

Confirmed standardPlace: "Benson, North Dakota, United States." Both network search tools timed out — working from loc_001's collections inventory plus known major FamilySearch census collections. Now writing the full plan in one batched call.
Fixing the plan shell — `rationale` is not a valid field on a plan entry.
Plan written — pl_001, 10 items. The invocation is `--autonomous`, so handing off to execution immediately.
Searching the 1900 US Federal Census for Spriggs in North Dakota — pli_001.

All 5 results are from a Grand Forks household (Ruben Spriggs, b. 1865 Minnesota) — a different family. No Spriggs found in Benson County. Logging this search and the orphaned staged search from the locality-guide agent, then trying name variants.
The orphaned search was from `external_links_search`. Fixing the tool field and retrying.
Logged. Now trying variant spelling "Sprigs" for the 1900 census in North Dakota.
Same Grand Forks household again — fuzzy matching treats "Sprigs" as "Spriggs." Now trying the specific Benson County 1900 census image group with the surname to search within that volume.

Confirmed: Benson County 1900 census image group is 0% name-indexed. Logging the unlogged "Sprigs" variant and the nil image group search, then trying a wildcard before escalating to the image browse.
One more wildcard variant before moving on — "Spri*" to catch completely different transcriptions.

115 results — no Spriggs in Benson County anywhere in the "Spri*" wildcard pool. Indexed search for the 1900 Benson County census is exhausted; the image browse fallback (pli_008) still needs execution via `search-images`. Logging and updating pli_001, then moving to the 1910 census.
Now searching the 1910 US Federal Census — pli_002. Reuben would be ~11 and almost certainly still in his parents' household.

Important find: a "Fred Sprigg" household in Albert Township, **Benson County** (township 17) in 1910, but none of the children match Reuben Spencer (born Nov 1898, ND — Fred's older children were born in Iowa). No "Reuben Spriggs" appears anywhere in the 28 ND results. Logging this search, then searching specifically for "Reuben" with surname variants to see if the family moved or is indexed differently.
Now searching for "Reuben" + "Spriggs" nationwide in the 1910 census — the family may have moved.

**Critical find!** Top match with `matchScore: 0.886` and `attachedToSubject: true` — **"Rueben S Spriggs"** (b. 1899, North Dakota) in the **household of John W Spriggs** in Prairie Belle, Beadle County, **South Dakota** in 1910. The family moved south by 1910. Reading the full household record now.

**Parents identified:** John W Spriggs (father, b. 1872, Iowa) and Charlotte Spriggs (mother, b. 1877, Norway). The family moved to South Dakota by 1910. Record already attached to subject. Logging this positive result and continuing with corroborating searches.
Now searching the 1920 census for John W Spriggs to corroborate and find the family together — pli_003.
The John Spriggs 1920 search didn't find him. Let me search for Reuben directly in 1920 to locate the family — he'd be ~21.
No Reuben in 1920 under that name. Let me search for John W Spriggs more broadly in 1920, and simultaneously search ND County Marriages for a Spriggs groom — pli_004.
Now searching ND County Marriages (pli_004, collection 2550852) for a Spriggs groom, and simultaneously broadening the 1920 census search for John W Spriggs.
No Spriggs marriage in ND collection 2550852. Let me log that nil and try broader — SD marriages and a broader 1920 census search for John W Spriggs.
Searching 1920 census for John W Spriggs (broader), and SD marriages for John Spriggs.

**Mother's maiden name found!** Multiple entries show **"John W Sprigg(s) and Charlotte/Charlotta Westby"** in Washington County Marriages (collection 1534448), with John's birth year 1872 matching perfectly. Reading the marriage record now to confirm details.

**Confirmed:** John W Sprigg + **Charlotta Westby** married **19 August 1898, Spokane, Washington** — just 79 days before Reuben's birth. Mother's maiden name: **Westby**. Also reveals her father: O. Westby; her mother's maiden name: Hansen. Logging all pending searches now.
Updating plan item statuses, then searching 1920 census for John W Spriggs specifically in South Dakota.
Not found in SD for 1920. Trying Iowa (where they were around 1900 based on Lillian's birthplace).
Logging the SD and Iowa 1920 nil searches and wrapping up the search phase — sufficient evidence has been gathered for extraction.

Search phase complete for the primary items. Here is what was found and needs extraction:

**Positive findings (two records ready for extraction):**

| Log | Record | Key finding |
|-----|--------|-------------|
| log_007 | 1910 US Census, Beadle Co., SD (`ark:/61903/1:1:MPXD-MZC`) | Reuben S Spriggs (b.1899 ND) in household of **John W Spriggs** (father, b.1872 Iowa) + **Charlotte Spriggs** (mother, b.1877 Norway). matchScore 0.886, already attached to subject. |
| log_012 | Washington County Marriages (`ark:/61903/1:1:QPMT-VPJ5`) | John W Sprigg + **Charlotta Westby** married **19 Aug 1898**, Spokane, WA. Mother's maiden name = **Westby**. Her parents: O. Westby (father), Hansen (mother's maiden name). |

**Search coverage so far (pl_001):**
- pli_001: in_progress (indexed search exhausted, image browse pli_008 still needed)
- pli_002: in_progress (positive — 1910 census found family in SD)
- pli_003: in_progress (1920 location not found; SD/Iowa nil)
- pli_004: in_progress (positive — marriage record found, Spokane WA)
- pli_005–010: not yet executed

Returning to the orchestrator — two positive records are unextracted and require `record-extraction`.
Two positive records unextracted. Routing to record-extraction for both.
Checking project state to see what the record-extractor agent produced before the context was lost.

No assertions written yet — the record-extractor agent did not complete. Resuming extraction now. Delegating 2 records; starting with Record 1 of 2: 1910 US Federal Census (Rueben S Spriggs, household of John W Spriggs).
Record 1 extracted: 39 assertions, src_001/S1 created. Now delegating Record 2 of 2: Washington County Marriages — John W Sprigg + Charlotta Westby, 19 August 1898.
Both records extracted — 39 + 22 = 61 assertions across two sources. Routing to person-evidence to link extracted assertions to tree persons.
Person-evidence complete. Parentage established in tree: I1 (John W Spriggs) and I2 (Charlotte Westby Spriggs) → L64C-QQX. Running log-vs-assertion cross-check before routing to exhaustiveness.

Log cross-check clean: log_001 is an administrative survey (no persona record to extract); log_007 and log_012 both extracted ✓; all 12 negative entries need no assertions. Routing to research-exhaustiveness — two independent records now establish parentage for q_001 even with plan items still open.

Not yet exhaustive — the Benson County birth-jurisdiction gap is open and pli_008 (1900 census image browse) is the critical outstanding item. Updating completed plan item statuses before routing to search-images.
pli_001, pli_002, pli_004 marked completed. Routing to search-images for pli_008 — the 1900 Benson County census image browse, the critical gap the exhaustiveness agent identified.
Maddock Township farming district browsed — no Spriggs found, but 214 images remain uncovered. Continuing image browse from image 004120517_00394.

Image browse capped at 20 images/film — Maddock Township farming rows covered, village rows not reachable automatically. Logging as a manual-browse gap and continuing with remaining plan items. Routing to search-records for pli_003 (1920 census), pli_007 (1915 ND state census), pli_005 (Lutheran church records), pli_006 (ND birth registration), and pli_010 (naturalization records).
Executing five remaining plan items in sequence. Starting with pli_003 — 1920 US Federal Census, nationwide search for Reuben Spriggs (b.~1898-1899, North Dakota).
All 10 results are wrong persons — birthplaces (Kansas, Texas, WV, etc.) don't match; no ND-born Reuben. Logging and trying variant spelling "Sprigg".
Same pool, no matches. Logging and trying father-centered search (John W Spriggs, b.~1872 Iowa) as a household anchor.
Only a city directory entry for J C Sprigg — not our person. Logging batch and moving to pli_007 (1915 ND State Census).
Now searching pli_007 — 1915 ND State Census. Testing whether image group 007637091_003_M9VK-5YC is name-indexed.
Zero results — vol. 1 is 0% indexed for this surname. Testing vol. 2 (007637092).
Vol. 2 has 8 indexed results — all Fred E Spriggs household (different family noted in log_006). No John W Spriggs. Checking ND-wide 1915 census.
Single result is Roy J Spriggs in Grand Forks — not our person. John W Spriggs not in ND 1915. Batch-logging all three pli_007 searches, then moving to pli_005.
Updating pli_007 to in_progress, then searching pli_005 — Lutheran church records (Flora and Esmond, Benson County).
Both volumes zero for Spriggs indexed portion. Trying "Westby" surname (mother's maiden name) in the same volumes.

Westby hit is a 1921 baptism for a different Westby family (Louis + Lillian Westby — not Charlotte). No Spriggs baptism in indexed portion. Batch-logging pli_005 and updating status; moving to pli_006.
Searching pli_006 — North Dakota birth registration for Reuben Spriggs born 1898.
**Significant hit — matchScore 0.766:** "Ruben Spencer Spriggs," baptism 6 Nov 1898, Lutheran church records. Reading the full record from the sidecar for parent names.

**Critical corroboration found.** The record names **J W Spriggs (father)** and **Charlotte Spriggs (mother)** for Ruben Spencer Spriggs — exactly matching our established parentage. This is FHL microfilm 100,881,426 (a third Lutheran church volume not in pli_005's list). Note: the index has birth/baptism dates reversed (baptism 6 Nov, birth 24 Nov — likely transposed by the indexer; original image needed). Place "Carrington, SD" is a geocoding error for Carrington, Foster County, ND.

Logging and routing immediately to extraction — this is a third independent record directly naming both parents.
Now searching pli_010 — Benson County naturalization records. Trying name search first even though locality guide says 0% indexed; if nil, full-text search will be needed.
Confirmed 0% indexed as expected. Logging pli_010 nil and wrapping up this search-records invocation.

Search phase complete. Here is the summary:

**Searches completed this invocation (logs 017–028):**

| Log | Plan item | Result |
|-----|-----------|--------|
| log_017 | pli_003 | Negative — Reuben Spriggs nationwide 1920 census: 10 results, all wrong persons |
| log_018 | pli_003 | Negative — "Sprigg" variant 1920 census: 12 results, same wrong pool |
| log_019 | pli_003 | Negative — John Spriggs + Charlotte, Iowa birth, 1920: city directory only |
| log_020 | pli_007 | Negative — 1915 ND state census Benson Co. vol. 1 (007637091): 0% indexed |
| log_021 | pli_007 | Negative — 1915 ND state census Benson Co. vol. 2 (007637092): Fred E Spriggs family only, not our John W |
| log_022 | pli_007 | Negative — ND-wide 1915 census, John Spriggs b.1867–1877: 1 wrong result (Roy J Spriggs, Grand Forks) |
| log_023–026 | pli_005 | Negative — Flora/Esmond Lutheran indexed portion (100881427, 100881428): 0 Spriggs; 3 Westby results in 100881428 but a different Westby family (Louis + Lillian Westby, 1921) |
| **log_027** | **pli_006** | **POSITIVE — "Ruben Spencer Spriggs," ELCA Lutheran records, FHL 100,881,426: Father = J W Spriggs, Mother = Charlotte Spriggs; baptism 6 Nov 1898, birth index shows 24 Nov 1898 (dates appear reversed — image needed); place "Carrington SD" is a geocoding error for Carrington, Foster County ND** |
| log_028 | pli_010 | Negative — naturalization records 0% indexed; fulltext_search needed |

**Key finding:** The Lutheran baptism record (log_027) is a third independent source directly naming both parents — J W Spriggs (father) and Charlotte Spriggs (mother) — for Ruben Spencer Spriggs. This substantially strengthens the parentage case.

**pli_009** (BLM homestead patents at glorecords.blm.gov) is an external site — routing to search-external-sites is needed for that item.

**pli_010** (naturalization records): 0% name-indexed; fulltext_search of volumes 007785641–007785645 is the next step — outside this skill's scope.

No assertions exist yet for log_027. Returning to orchestrator for record-extraction of the Lutheran baptism record and external-site search for pli_009.

---
Delegating 1 record: the ELCA Lutheran baptism entry for Ruben Spencer Spriggs (log_027).

The 1898 ELCA Lutheran baptism register index names Ruben Spencer Spriggs as being baptized, with J W Spriggs listed as his father and Charlotte Spriggs as his mother, in Carrington, Foster County, North Dakota (the index incorrectly says "South Dakota" — Carrington is in North Dakota). The index dates are almost certainly transposed by whoever created it: a baptism on November 6 and a birth on November 24 is impossible, so the birth is recorded here as November 6, 1898 and the baptism as November 24, 1898, with a note that the original church register image must be checked to confirm. This is a FamilySearch index of the original register, not the register itself, so the original has not been examined.

The next step is to view the original register image at ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C9PT-V9Q2-2 to confirm the correct birth and baptism dates, check whether the father's full given name appears, and verify whether Charlotte's maiden name is recorded — then proceed to proof-conclusion for q_001.

---

Returning to orchestrator. src_003/S3 written with 9 assertions (a_061–a_069). Now routing to person-evidence to link the new assertions, then will handle pli_009 (BLM external site) and pli_010 (naturalization full-text).
Three independent records now corroborate the parentage. Consulting research-exhaustiveness — the Lutheran baptism record substantially closes the Benson County geographic gap.
Clear action list from exhaustiveness. Closing out the four completable/skippable items first, then loading fulltext_search schema for pli_010.
Launching fulltext search for pli_010 and church image read in parallel, while handling pli_009 via search-external-sites.

Fulltext search negative for vol. 1; image inaccessible (network error). Logging results, completing pli_010 (John was Iowa-born/US citizen; Charlotte auto-naturalized through marriage — no petition expected), then routing pli_009 to external-sites.
Now routing pli_009 — BLM General Land Office homestead patent search — to search-external-sites.

pli_009 targets the BLM General Land Office — a non-FamilySearch government site not in the standard external-sites enum. Generating the search URL manually and logging as an awaitingUser entry.

The search URLs for glorecords.blm.gov to find Spriggs land patents in North Dakota:

- **Spriggs surname, ND:** https://glorecords.blm.gov/results/default.aspx#searchCriteria=sfs%5B0%5D%3DSearchByType%3D1%26sfs%5B1%5D%3DSTATE_ABV%3DND%26sfs%5B2%5D%3DPATENTEE_SURNAME%3DSpriggs
- **Sprigg variant, ND:** https://glorecords.blm.gov/results/default.aspx#searchCriteria=sfs%5B0%5D%3DSearchByType%3D1%26sfs%5B1%5D%3DSTATE_ABV%3DND%26sfs%5B2%5D%3DPATENTEE_SURNAME%3DSprigg
Re-evaluating exhaustiveness for q_001 — all plan items are now resolved (completed/skipped/logged awaiting capture).

pli_009 is still `planned` in the plan — the log entry was written but the plan item status was never updated. I'll formally skip it (BLM land record is corroborating-only; URL already handed to user; parentage established by three independent sources), then attempt the ELCA baptism image one more time before re-invoking exhaustiveness.
pli_009 formally skipped. Now re-invoking research-exhaustiveness — all plan items are now in terminal states.
Exhaustiveness declared. Now invoking proof-conclusion for q_001.

Score them with the project-relative form, which assembles both documents for you: `same_person({ projectPath, assertionId, treePersonId: "I7" })`. `assertionId` is the assertion the link cites. The tool resolves the record itself and builds the tree side as that person's matching mob, so you hand-build nothing (person-evidence, 'Call it with references, not documents'). If this call was denied, the entire batch was rejected — including any ops in other sections — and must be re-issued after the same_person call. A relationship or marriage assertion names two parties and gets a link for each. The call is about the assertion's own `record_role` party by default; for the OTHER party add `recordRole` (or `recordPersonaId`) naming it. Reusing the first party's persona for the second is how a near-zero score gets manufactured and then explained away. If the tool answers that the record holds no persona for that party, or that the candidate is a stub minted from the very persona you would be scoring (circular), say so in the link's `rationale` and proceed — the gap is still recorded; the rationale is the record of why, not a waiver. How the assertion was RETRIEVED is not such a case: a full-text hit, an image, a PDF and a sidecar-less search are all scorable, because the tool derives the record side from the record's own assertions when it cannot fetch a document. A locally-minted tree id is NOT such a case: it scores on document content and must be scored.
